_README: Posts that were PUBLISHED ON PRODUCTION and only later adopted into git.
For these, git answers the wrong question. A post's first commit is the date
SOMEONE COPIED IT INTO THE REPO, not the date it went live. gen-sitemap.py:122
already knew this ('an adoption changes when a file last moved in history
without touching a byte the reader sees') while check-schema-dates.py was built
on the opposite premise. This file is where the two stop contradicting each
other: the checker reads the expected datePublished FROM HERE for these paths,
and from git for everything else.
WHO WRITES IT: whoever performs an adoption, in the same commit as the adoption.
An adoption with no entry here is a post whose datePublished nothing can verify.
WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT: independent evidence that the value is TRUE. The
datePublished below is the production page's own claim, which is also what the
HTML says — so the checker's comparison is a declaration-vs-artifact match, not
a derivation. Its job is to make DRIFT visible and to stop fix-schema-dates.py
overwriting a true date with a false one. Independence comes from
`evidence.first_serve_utc`: an access-log row proving the page was served before
the adopting commit existed. You cannot serve a file that does not exist.
KEYED BY REPO-RELATIVE PATH, never basename. blog/index.html and
how-to/index.html collapse to one string under a basename key, and the lane that
loses is silent.

_evidence_source.expires_approx: N/A for the banked copy — see _banking below
_evidence_source.note: Prod access logs, status 200 only. A 404 row proves NON-existence and must never mint a bound. Counts: buffet 14, cai-fan 14, intermittent-fasting 23, kopi 19, durian 25.
_banking: The 4-slug bound file (~/.openclaw-nori/workspace/evidence/adoption-logs/live-by.json)
and the 101-page corpus it was drawn from both lived in Nori's workspace at mode
0600, outside any repo, on a 30-day log rotation. Evidence with an expiry date is
not evidence a year from now, and a 0600 path is unreadable to every other agent
and to CI. The corpus is therefore BANKED IN-REPO at ../evidence/first-200-utc.json,
with ../evidence/derive-adoption-set.py to re-derive this whole file's population
from it. Both are outside the deploy allow-list (scripts/deploy.sh ends --exclude='*'
and only traverses /blog/, /how-to/, /mini/), so they are versioned, not published.
ONE BANKED COPY, NOT TWO. This field named ../evidence/first-serve-by-page.json
until 2026-07-22 — a second banking of the same 101-page capture, made in parallel
with Mochi's a069755 and holding a byte-equal `pages` payload (verified key-set and
value-wise, 101/101, 0 diffs, against a control that produced 1). It was deleted
rather than kept as a cross-check: two files with the same provenance are not two
instruments, they are one instrument that can now disagree with itself. The
surviving copy is the one check-schema-dates.py actually reads.
NAMING: the confusable pair was never two FILES. `state/live-by/live_by.json` does
not exist and never did. `live_by` is a FIELD — it is `pages[path].live_by` in the
real capture, whose `_what` header opens `live_by = UPPER BOUND on datePublished`.
A field name got read as the artifact's identity and written down as a path. The two
real artifacts are `state/live-by/first-serve-by-page.json` (101 pages, `pages`
schema, durian present) and `evidence/adoption-logs/live-by.json` (4 slugs, `bounds`
schema), both under ~/.openclaw-nori/workspace — different directory AND basename,
not one character apart. The banked copy is named for its load-bearing FIELD,
first_200_utc, and that convention is still right for a sharper reason than it was
adopted for: naming a file for its field is what stops a field becoming a filename.
See ../evidence/README.md.

blog/how-to-log-durian.html.note: STRONGEST OF THE FIVE, and it is the one that was missing. Served to a third party (Alibaba Cloud, curl/8.14.1 — same scraper family as buffet/cai-fan, and NOT our egress 103.11.50.23, so self_generated=false) 1414s BEFORE the adopting commit existed. It does not rest on one row: THREE non-egress serves precede the commit (14:32:05, 14:32:06, 14:37:00 UTC) and our own first curl is 14:52:12, still 20m before the commit. 25 rows, all 200, zero 404. State the gap in SECONDS: both instants fall on 2026-07-16, and that is precisely why the checker's calendar-day comparison `continue`d over this row — the entry was not flagged and not waved, it was ABSENT. WHY IT ESCAPED THE HAND-WRITTEN SET: this file was created 2026-07-22 in d80405a, five days after every adoption it describes, so the README's 'written in the same commit as the adoption' rule could not have been followed by ANY of these five — all were back-filled. The back-fill was transcribed from 96da7b0's commit body, whose `new:` line lists exactly the three that got entries; durian appears one line lower under `mod:` ('+133B vs d31cca9 rescue') because it had already been rescued 68 minutes earlier in its own commit. One commit's file list was read as if it were the population. The population is ../evidence/first-200-utc.json — re-derive it, do not transcribe it.

blog/how-to-log-a-buffet.html.note: Served to a third party (Alibaba Cloud, curl/8.14.1) 898s BEFORE the adopting commit. The git date is falsified, not merely doubted.

blog/how-to-log-cai-fan.html.note: Same 898s gap. State it in SECONDS — '16 Jul vs 17 Jul' is a midnight-SGT artifact (23:48 vs 00:03) and reporting it as a one-day gap re-imports the exact ambiguity this file exists to kill.

blog/how-to-log-kopi-and-teh.html.note: WEAKEST OF THE FOUR AND THE FIELD SAYS SO: the first serve is OUR OWN deploy-verification curl from our egress IP, so it is an existence proof but NOT independent (third_party=false). 2026-07-21 is the production page's own value and is the truer date - the post was live on the 21st. Do NOT 'fix' it to the adopting commit's date 2026-07-22; that falsifies content to green a broken instrument. This is the entry the old TZ bucket failed to spare, purely because the adoption ran at 11:08 instead of 00:03.
